newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Glickman says pessimistic on EU meat accord.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Glickman says pessimistic on EU meat accord.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said that he did not expect negotiators to settle a dispute with the European Union over meat and poultry inspection methods before a Tuesday deadline.
Speaking to reporters at an agricultural policy conference, Glickman declined to detail what actions the United States might take if no agreement was reached.
"There could be some major breakthrough tonight, although I don't expect it," Glickman said. "Presuming there is no agreement tonight, there will be an announcement (by USDA) tomorrow," he said.
Glickman also said that failure to reach an accord on the so-called veterinary equivalency dispute was likely to cause trade disruption, but he declined to elaborate.
Negotiators have met in Washington in recent days to try to resolve how the United States and the EU reconcile their different meat and poultry inspection methods.
An agreement would allow each side to accept products from the other even if their inspection methods differed.
The EU has said it would implement new veterinary and sanitary controls for imports on April 1, and the United States has said it would retaliate for any loss of access to EU markets.
Glickman said the EU and the United States each agreed on the need for stringent food safety regulations, but differed on "a remaining handful of issues."
"Unfortunately things do not look good for an agreement tomorrow," he said.

About $50 million worth of U.S. poultry shipments to the EU could be affected if the EU adopts new standards, and Washington could decide to halt the import of $200 million worth of EU pork, industry experts have said.
